GENERAL 
 
This manual  must be read and understood by persons responsible for installation 
and operation of the pump before it is installed and operated. Operators are 
responsible for following the provisions of this manual during each pump operation 
stage. 
 
The manufacturer „Hydro-Vacuum” S.A. does not take any responsibility for  if the 
pump is operated in conditions other than conditions approved by the manufacturer in 
writing.  
 
This guarantee does not apply if  the provisions of this manual are breached, in 
particular in case the device is operated outside its intended use or in an incorrect 
manner or the pump is dismantled in an unauthorised manner. The warranty does not 
cover natural wear and tear of the pump and its wear parts, i.e.: impeller, seals, shaft, 
protective sleeves, bearings, slip rings, etc. or damage occurred during shipment.

2.  
SAFETY 
2.1. 
Symbols used in the manual 
 
The manual contains the following symbols regarding safety of operation and 
device: 
 
General danger symbol specifically regarding operation of the pumping 
unit –  failure to comply with these warnings  may result in endangering 
personnel's life or  health! 
 
ATTENTION! 
Safety note - in particular regarding correct pump operation - failure to 
comply with these warnings may lead to damage of the device! 
 
 
A warning regarding a voltage presence – failure to comply with these 
warnings may result in an electric shock or damage. 
 
 
Marking of explosion protection 
Symbol indicates information on explosion protection in  areas with 
danger of explosions, in accordance with  2014/34 UE (ATEX). 
2.2. 
General informations 
NHVf series pumps  comply with the requirements of Machine Directive 2006/42/EG. 
 
The personnel employed to install, operate, inspect and maintain the 
device, must prove they have sufficient knowledge on safety 
regulations, have all required qualifications as well as know and comply 
with instructions provided in this manual. 
 
ATTENTION! 
The pump unit must not be operated in a manner contrary to its 
intended use as regards physical-chemical properties of the pumped 
medium, i.e. capacity, pressure, temperature, density, aggressiveness, 
abrasion, rotational speed direction and value as well as other 
parameters defined in pump technical data or offer details. If a pump is 
to be used for a different application, contact a sales office or 
manufacturer's representative. Hydro-Vacuum S.A. shall not be 
responsible in case a pump is used for other purposes without its prior 
explicit consent provided in writing.

3 
 
ATTENTION! 
The pump unit must not be operated within an installation constructed 
contrary to the art of engineering, in particular as regards the design of 
the suction and delivery line and ensuring the permissible operating 
field and temperature. 
 
ATTENTION! 
The operator is responsible for maintaining the pump unit in a proper 
technical condition, prompt inspections and replacement of worn-out 
parts. It is forbidden to activate the pumping engine when it is 
dismantled or not connected to the installation. 
2.3. 
Safety regulations 
The manual contains basic requirements that must be complied with during 
installation, operation, inspections and repairs of the pump and pumping unit.  
The pump operating manual must always be located in a visible and accessible 
location in the operation area. In case the pump or pumping unit is moved or 
transferred to a third person, the manual must be delivered to the end-user. 
This manual does not refer to general accident prevention regulations and does not 
take into account local industrial safety and legal regulations that must be applied. 
This manual does not include information regarding protective devices and 
methods of recycling of the pumped medium and/or media used to rinse or lubricate 
bearings, in particular as regards their toxicity. Personnel is responsible for correct 
operation of the pumping motor, in line with applicable regulations. 
2.4. 
Consequences and threats resulting from failure to comply with safety  
 
 
instructions 
• 
Failure to comply with this operating manual results in loss of rights arising out of 
 
the warranty and liability for damages. 
• 
Failure to comply with this manual may lead to the following risks: 
 
Risks for personnel resulting from impact exerted by an electric field, 
magnetic field, high temperatures, mechanical and chemical impact as 
well as explosion.  
Risk for environment  from leakage of dangerous substances. 
 
ATTENTION! 
Failure of important product functions. 
Failure of measuring devices and electronic equipment resulting from 
magnetic field impact.

4 
 
 
Risk of explosion especially for products for use in hazardous areas. 
Products for use in hazardous areas must be compatible and properly 
marked. It is recommended to observe relevant instructions 
2.5. 
Personnel safety 
 
Failure to comply with any of the following provisions results in risks to 
personnel's health or life and property damage. 
• 
Usage of product components depends on individual operating conditions thus the 
 
operator must ensure regular inspections and maintenance. In case any 
 
irregularities regarding the product condition or abnormal operating parameters are 
 
noticed, the pump must be immediately stopped. Otherwise, the product may be 
 
damaged and, in particular, personnel safety is compromised. 
• 
Personnel must have and use appropriate personal protective equipment. 
• 
As regards systems or products whose damage may result in endangering 
 
personnel's safety or life, it must be equipped with alarm devices which are 
 
constantly in the standby mode. 
• 
In case of systems or products used to pump low or high temperature liquids which 
 
may cause injuries, these systems must be protected against accidental contact 
 
and marked as applicable 
• 
Moving elements of the pump or pump unit must be protected against accidental 
 
contact by providing necessary guards. Do not disassemble moving element 
 
guards during device operation. An exception from this rule is the procedure of 
 
adjusting the packing gland which must be conducted by qualified personnel. After 
 
the procedure is completed, guards must always be reassembled. 
• 
In case of pumps or systems whose noise emission level exceeds 85 dB, personnel 
 
must use applicable hearing protection measures. 
• 
Leakage (e.g. sealings) dangerous (e.g. toxic agents, explosive, hot or cold 
 
substances) must be handled in a manner safe for personnel and the environment. 
 
Always observe all applicable legal regulations. 
 
Threat connected with electricity must be eliminated on the basis of local 
regulations regarding electric equipment. During work conducted on 
electric equipment, it must be effectively isolated from the supply source 
by deactivating a switch and removing a fuse or permanently isolated and 
secured against accidental activation.

5 
2.6. 
Maintenance, inspection and repair works safety 
 
Failure to comply with any of the following provisions results in risks to 
personnel's health or life and property damage. 
• 
Any work on the pumping unit must be conducted by authorised and qualified 
 
personnel familiar with the content of this manual. 
• 
Any work on the pumping unit must be conducted during its standstill, in line with 
 
the following rules: 
- 
Secure the unit against unintentional power-up. 
- 
Internal pump pressure must be equal to the ambient pressure. 
- 
The pump should be emptied of pumped medium. 
- 
Temperature of unit elements must be equal to the ambient temperature. 
- 
In case dangerous substances are pumped, internal elements of the pump 
  
and auxiliary systems must be disinfected. 
- 
Immediately after work is completed, reassemble and activate all protective 
  
and safety devices in their mounting locations. 
ATTENTION! 
Failure to comply with any of the following provisions results in risks to 
correct device operation. 
• 
Any work on a pumping unit still covered by a warranty must be conducted by an 
 
authorised manufacturer's service department or with its written consent. After the 
 
warranty period expires, it is recommended that any work, in particular repair works 
 
activities, should be conducted by an authorised manufacturer's service department..  
• 
Any modification of the pump or pumping unit is permitted only subject to 
 
manufacturer's written consent. 
• 
Parts used to conduct work on the unit must be genuine and approved by the 
 
manufacturer. Using unauthorised parts results in warranty becoming void and all 
 
related consequences.  
2.7. 
Safety of use in hazardous areas 
 
Operating pump unit  in explosion hazardous areas is permissible in 
accordance with the operation and maintenance manual and the 
following instructions. 
 
 
Products used in explosion hazardous areas must be compatible and  
properly marked.  
Explosion protection is ensured if the product is used as intended only. 
The pump unit must not operate outside its performance limits.

6

Marking on the pump applies only to the specific pump.  
The coupling and the motor should have separate markings and should be

2.7.2. Operating temperature 
 
In normal conditions, the highest temperature may occur at the pump 
casing and the bearing mount surface, as well as the shaft packing and 
the external mechanical seal system, if used.  
The temperature at the pump casing surface corresponds to the medium 
temperature. 
For pumps with heating jacket, please observe the relevant system 
temperature class. 
The temperature class  presents a maximum temperature value at the pump unit 
surface permitted for use with medium at the maximum limit temperature. Permissible 
temperature class  is displayed on the pump data plate. Detailed data on maximum 
permissible medium temperature appears in offer documentation or data sheet.

2.7.3. Filling the pump and system 
 
In order to prevent the explosive atmosphere from forming when 
transferring flammable media, make sure the pump and lines are filled 
with the medium at all times.  
If the pump and the lines cannot be filled with medium at all times, use 
suitable monitoring (e.g. inlet pressure measurement, medium level 
sensor) to prevent dry run and temperature rise above the permissible 
limits.

8 
2.7.4. Checking motor direction 
Motor should rotate clockwise as viewed from the motor side. It is recommended 
check motor direction with coupling halves decoupled. Otherwise, check motor 
direction by running the pump unit connected to the system and filled with medium for 
several seconds.  
 
It is prohibited run the pump unit without connecting it to the system and 
filling with medium. Dry run may lead to a rise in temperature above its 
permissible limit, explosion and damage to pump components. 
2.7.5. Pump start-up and operation 
Pump can be started after all conditions in section 6 are met, and all precautions 
are taken for the pumps for use in hazardous areas. 
 
Before start-up, fully open the suction line valve and open the discharge 
line valve approximately 25%. Immediately after start-up, set the valve to 
enable operation within its performance limits. 
Pump can also be started with the discharge line valve open if other 
adjustment methods are used, i.e. frequency inverter. 
 
 
It is prohibited to run the pump with suction and/or discharge line valve 
closed to prevent rapid rise in temperature. 
 
 
For pumps with mechanical seals, the temperature may rise above its limit 
value near the shaft packing due to the dry run conditions. Dry run may be 
due to: 
• 
incorrect installation and running without medium, 
• 
transferring medium with high gas content, 
• 
pump operation outside its performance limits, 
• 
incorrect suction line configuration. 
2.7.6. Apparatus and additional devices 
 
It is prohibited to install electrical devices, control devices and accessories 
(e.g. mechanical seal system) which does not meet all relevant safety and 
explosion protection requirements.

9 
2.7.7. Maintenance 
 
Ensure correct maintenance and inspect the pump components on regular 
basis to avoid excessive temperature rise or loss of integrity of 
components, i.e. bearings, shaft. 
The pump unit must be kept clean and in good working condition to 
ensure proper heat exchange with its surroundings. 
2.8. 
Operating safety 
ATTENTION! 
  
The pump unit must not be operated in a manner incompatible with 
physical-chemical properties of the pumped medium, i.e. output, 
pressure, temperature, density, aggressiveness, abrasion, rotational 
speed as well as other parameters defined in pump technical data, 
offer details or other written arrangements with a manufacturer's 
representative. 
2.9. 
Hazards resulting from temperature, pressure, flow and rotational speed 
ATTENTION! 
The user must ensure correct safety measures in the installation are 
provided so that temperature, pressure and rotational speed does not 
exceed applicable (minimum or maximum) limit values, permissible 
values or values that have been individually arranged. 
Water hammer – In particular, the pump must be protected against 
results of its sudden stopping and possible water hammer impact. Thus 
it is recommended that, e.g. a check valve, tank with an air cushion, etc. 
should be used. Failure to fulfil this condition results in destroying the 
pump flow system and may result in housing damage. 
System NPSH – In particular, the pump must be protected against 
excessive pressure drops in the suction pipeline below the NPSHr value 
plus a reserve equal to at least 10% of the NPSHr value, however, not 
less than 0.5 m. The required NPSHr value is individually specified for 
each operating point and provided in the operation characteristics. 
Failure to fulfil this condition results in cavitation in the pump, 
compromising the pump parameters and hydraulic system damage.

10 
 
ATTENTION! 
Thermal shock – In particular, ensure sudden temperature fluctuations 
are avoided as they may result in a thermal shock that may damage the 
pump. 
Reverse flow – In particular, it is necessary to protect the pump against 
reverse flow as it may result in increase of revolutions exceeding the 
permissible range and occurrence of tension on the electric motor 
terminals. Thus check valves must be used. 
Minimum flow – To avoid the risk of pump operation with a valve 
closed on the pumping side for a period longer that several seconds or 
hot water circulation, the system must be equipped with an installation 
ensuring minimum flow through the pump is maintained. 
 
3.  
DESCRIPTION NHVf TYPE PUMPS 
3.1. 
Construction and operating principles 
NHVf pumps are centrifugal single stage torque pumps. The pumps transfer 
mechanical energy of the rotating impeller to the medium present between its vanes. 
The centrifugal pumps cannot self-prime (transfer air through the pump and the suction 
line), and must be filled before every run. 
NHVf type single stage centrifugal impeller pump with horizontal axis features a 
spiral channel with horizontal inlet (pump flows through the suction port) and a vertical 
discharge port (with axis corresponding to the pump axis). A centrifugal impeller is 
mounted inside the pump casing and fastened to the pump shaft with nuts. 
The pump shaft is mounted on the bearings in the bearing mount using grease or 
oil lubricated rolling bearings The pump is driven by an 50/60 Hz asynchronous motor 
at a rated speed of approx. 1000, 1450 and 2950 rpm (other models available 
depending on the intended use of pump unit i.e in marine versions , explosion-proof or 
with diesel motor). 
The pump shaft is sealed with a cord seal  or mechanical seal (single or double), 
lubricated and cooled with medium  
The pump is mounted on the frame with lugs on the suction casing and the 
bearing casing. 
Overall dimensions and rated parameters conform to z EN 733. 
Suction and discharge inlets conform to ISO 7005-2/PN 16. 
All impellers are balanced static and dynamic ISO 1940 class 6.3.

13 
3.2. 
Applications 
 
NHVf pumps are used for pumping clean or low solids content media (maximum 
solids content 20 mg/dm3) at up to 140ºC, within the strength limits of materials used in 
production.  Main applications: 
• 
Industrial installations , pressure boosting , fire-extinguishing systems; 
• 
Water systems, residential or drinking water, 
• 
Irrigation and drainage systems, 
• 
Fire extinguishing systems; 
• 
Power engineering.

4.  
UNPACKING, TRANSPORT AND STORAGE 
4.1. 
Unpacking 
• 
After receiving the product, check if it complies with the waybill. 
• 
Check if the packaging has not been visibly damaged during transport. 
• 
Carefully remove the packing material. Check for any scratches or damage of the 
pump and other equipment (if any) that may result from improper transport. 
• 
In case any damage is detected, report it immediately to the Customer Service 
Department. 
4.2. 
Transport 
4.2.1. General recommendations 
 
• Keep strictly any applicable accident prevention regulations. 
• During transport, always use protective gloves, helmets and boots with 
metal toe protectors. 
• Wooden boxes, crates or cartons may be unloaded by means of 
forklifts or gantry cranes, depending on the packaging size, weight and 
design. 
4.2.2. Lifting 
• 
Before lifting and moving a pump, or a pump with a motor on a common base,  
 
always define: 
 
- 
total weight and position of the centre of gravity; 
 
- 
the maximum outside dimensions; 
 
- 
location of the lifting eyes. 
• 
The lifting capacity of lifting equipment must comply with the pump or pumping  
 
unit weight. 
• 
Both the pump and the pump unit must be lifted horizontally. 
• 
It is absolutely forbidden to stay under suspended loads or in their vicinity. 
• 
A load must never be suspended longer than it is absolutely necessary. 
• 
Acceleration and braking during lifting operations must be safe for persons. 
Lift the pump or the pump unit as shown in Fig. 4.1a and 4.1b to avoid obstacles 
(do not use motor lugs to lift the entire pump unit).

4.3. 
Storage 
• 
If a pump is to be mounted and commissioned right after delivery, it must be stored 
in a clean, dry room, protected against frost and ensuring moderate temperature 
fluctuations. 
• 
If a pump is equipped with bearings which require lubrication, apply an extra layer 
of grease in order to avoid moisture penetration into the area around the shaft. 
• 
The pump must be adequately secured against moisture, dust, dirt and foreign 
bodies.  
• 
The pump shaft must be periodically turned (for example once a week), to avoid 
bearing surface pitting and pump seizure. 
 
 
5.  
ON-SITE INSTALLATION 
ATTENTION! 
The device must be installed in accordance with the regulations. 
The pump may be installed, levelled and adjusted only by experienced 
personnel. Faulty installation or incorrect foundations may result in 
operation issues not covered by the warranty.

20 
5.1. 
Pump with shaft without cover 
• 
If a pump is delivered with a uncovered shaft end, it is necessary to prepare a 
correct plate on which the pumping unit with a motor is to be installed. The base 
plate must be designed and constructed in a manner ensuring necessary stiffness

5.5. 
Connecting a pipeline 
5.5.1. General 
ATTENTION! 
It is not allowed in any case to use a pump as an anchoring point or 
support for a pipeline. 
 
• 
Pipes should be supported very close to the pump (Fig. 5.4a and 5.4b). Make sure 
that pipeline loads and tensions are not transferred to the pump. Thus, after 
pipeline installation, loosen the suction and discharge flange bolts to prevent stress 
transfer from the line to the pump. 
• 
Nominal measures of flanges on the discharge and suction side are not reference 
points for selecting correct dimensions of the suction and discharge pipelines. 
Nominal pipe diameters should be equal or larger than the pump housing 
dimensions. Do not use pipes and accessories with diameter lower than the pump 
port diameter. Select the foot valves, strainers, filters and check valves with higher 
flow areas. Generally, linear flow rate shall not exceed 2 m/s at the suction line and 
3 m/s at the discharge line. Higher flow rates will increase pressure drops, which 
may result in cavitation at the suction line and friction losses at the discharge line. 
• 
Pipes must be connected by means of flanges with seals of correct size and made 
of appropriate materials. A flange seal must be located centrally between flange 
bolts, such a way that the opening is not obstructed.   
• 
Take into account thermal expansion and excessive pipeline vibrations so that their 
effects are not transferred on the pump. 
• 
The pipe must be cleaned from welding residues, sand, rust and possible hurds, 
which may be deposited therein. Plug the pump inlets in order to prevent dirt 
penetration After the system is assembled, all pipeline parts must be dismounted, 
thoroughly cleaned, painted and reassembled. If a sieve is used on the suction 
side, it should be cleaned after several days of operation. 
 
ATTENTION! 
It is recommended to use supports and expansion joints on the suction 
line and discharge lines, in order to reduce stresses on the system.

The pump installation may be activated only be personnel trained in

also be familiar with applicable local regulations. 
6.1. 
Preparation for start-up 
• 
Standard NHVf pumps  are equipped with sealed bearing which are filled with a 
grease for a whole operating time. In case of pumps equipped with open bearings 
check for fouling during transport or installation before first run. 
• 
Check the level of the pumped medium in the pump. NHVf pumps and suction line 
must be primed with medium. 
• 
Check if elements rotate freely and evenly. 
• 
Check if the pump, motor, coupling guard as well as other additional and protective 
devices have been installed correctly. 
• 
Check if the suction line valve is open, the discharge line valve must be opened 
approx. 25% (pumps up to 30 kW can be run with the discharge line valve 
temporarily closed). 
• 
Check if the electrical connections are made correctly. 
• 
Turn the pump on/off for a short time to check the rotation direction. Motor should 
rotate clockwise as viewed from the drive side.

After commissioning:

Define the pump operation set point in line with the data plate or data provided in 
the order form 
ATTENTION!
 
Operation with a closed valve on the suction or discharge side is 
forbidden as it may result in excessive increase in temperature and 
vibrations resulting in pump damage. 
• 
While commissioning the pump with an empty discharge pipeline, until the pipeline 
 
is fully filled, partly close the discharge valve so that the pump operates within the 
 
permissible operating range.  
ATTENTION! 
Operation with an empty discharge pipeline may result in excessive 
increase in output, which causes motor overloading, cavitation and 
increased vibrations.

the  leakage tighten evenly the screws fixing the gland seal.

Access to gland pacing requires removing the cover. Special care 
should be taken during regulations, long hair should be tied and hidden, 
clothes should not be loose-fitting , its creating the risk of  incidental 
drawing them in on a shaft.  
After regulations mount the cover. 
 
ATTENTION! 
Incorrect adjustment of gland seal or lack of it causes damage to 
sealing cord and shaft protecting sleeves,  increase of power input or

7.  
SERVICE AND MAINTENANCE 
 
Any servicing must be carried out by a trained and experience 
personnel familiar with the content of this operation and maintenance 
manual. 
 Make sure the pump unit's power supply is disconnected and protected 
against accidental activation before commencing any works on the 
pump unit. 
Wait for the pump casing temperature to reach ambient temperature for 
high or low temperature medium. 
 
Close the discharge and inflow line valve and equalize the pump and ambient 
pressure and drain the medium before disassembly. 
 
For corrosive or hazardous media, rinse the pump with inert fluid or 
decontaminate and dispose of the medium and washings in accordance 
with relevant regulations. 
Drain the bearing casing in pumps with oil lubricated bearings. 
 
In potentially explosive atmospheres it is prohibited to use tool which 
usage may lead to sparks and fire, use non-sparking tools only. 
 
ATTENTION! 
The manufacturer recommends use of genuine spare parts  
purchased from an authorized service centres or directly from the 
manufacturer. Compare replaced and new parts and make sure they 
are identical and made of the same materials. 
 
 
The bearing retainer in pumps for use in potentially explosive  areas,  
should be inspected daily for excessive heat and noise, as well as 
grease or oil condition. Change grease or oil immediately after 
observing any wear to the bearings. 
 
 
 
During work observe safety regulations and secure the pump and its components 
against accidental falls. 
 
During the disassembly of the pump as a result of seal damage, it is recommended 
to check all other components, e.g. bearings and replace if necessary. 
 
The components must be cleaned, and all mating surfaces must be degreased and 
smooth.

40 
 
The required bolt torque values must be respected. 
 
Installation and mating surfaces may be smeared with inert substance e.g. soap to 
facilitate installation. 
7.1. 
Gland with soft sealing 
 
Gland with soft sealing requires permanent supervision  which should be expressed 
by checking the amount of  leaking liquid. Correct leakage through gland seal should 
amount to 60-90 per minute. 
ATTENTION! 
Liquid from gland seal most not flowing  and water vapour should not 
get outside,  as this could result in burns. 
 
 
Slight leakage may cause overheating of gland seal, damage of cord 
and damage of shaft protecting sleeves. Major leakage may cause 
excessive increase of vibrations and pump bearing  can be flooded. 
 
If further gland seal regulation is not possible, packing should be replaced with new 
one. Work only when pump is stopped and when there’s no working medium. 
 
When pumping aggressive liquids rinse pump before dismantling the 
sealing. 
 
Cut the ends of cord at an angle 45º and lay it in gland seal turned 90º, The cord 
length should be adjusted so that there’s no gaps between its ends. Before pump 
commissioning with new seal packing lightly tighten using gland seal  without causing 
shaft locking. After start-up adjust leakage to amount ~60 drops per minute and install  
the seal shield. 
7.2. 
Gland with mechanical sealing 
Mechanical seal of the pump fully reduces leakages. In case they are noticed, it 
means that it has been damaged. 
As a rule, gland with mechanical seal are maintenance-free. Maintenance of 
specialist packing equipped with support systems must be conducted in line with 
packing manufacturer's recommendations and the manual provided.  
See section 8 for packing replacement procedures. 
Mechanical seals can be used only when the pump is primed with liquid.

41 
 
ATTENTION! 
Mechanical seal must not be dry-operated as it results in their 
immediate damage. 
 
 
When packing is replaced, drain liquid from the pump and, if the liquid is 
aggressive, rinse with warm water. All activities must be conducted 
during standstill, after the unit is secured against unintentional 
activation. 
 
During new packing installation, thoroughly clean the chamber. In order to facilitate 
the process on inserting the packing on the shaft and housing, they may be covered 
with soapy water. Do not touch the frictional surfaces of sliding rings. In case any 
contamination is noticed, remove it with acetone. Prior to installation, check the sealing 
rings for visible scratches. In case any irregularities are detected, replace the packing 
with new one that is free of flaws.  
 
Depending on the application, NHVf pumps are also available with different seal 
types. 
7.3. 
Bearings 
As a standard, NHVf series pumps come with rolling bearings lubricated with solid 
grease. Bearing versions lubricated with oil are also available. The minimum design life 
of bearings is 20,000 h. After this time, bearings must be replaced. 
In hot water pumps, bearings made of bearing steel for operation in high 
temperatures are used.  
ATTENTION! 
Bearing temperature may exceed ambient temperature by 50ºC.  
Do not exceed ambient temperature by 80ºC 
 
 
The bearing housing in pumps for use in potentially explosive areas,  
should be inspected daily for excessive heat and noise, as well as 
grease or oil condition. Change grease or oil immediately after 
observing any wear to the bearings. 
 
For oil lubricated pumps, check oil level in the bearings and top up as necessary.At 
least once a year, drain the spent oil and refill with new oil, up to the indicated level.

7.4. 
Coupling 
 
Regularly (every 1000 hours) check the gap between coupling elements and unit 
alignment. In case there is misalignment, re-align the unit (Table 5.1). 
ATTENTION! 
 
Check coupling components (inserts, rubber etc.) every 1000 hours, 
replace worn components and check unit alignment. 
7.5. 
Maintaining the pump cleanliness 
 
Presence of large amounts of dust and dirt on external surfaces of the 
pump results in its incorrect cooling and may cause excessive 
temperature increase. 
 
ATTENTION! 
Always keep the pump clean. Do not use pressurised water to clean 
the pump as it may penetrate the rolling bearing housings

8.  
DISASSEMBLY, REPAIRS AND REASSEMBLY 
8.1. 
General 
 
All service and maintenance activities concerning a pumping unit must 
be conducted only by trained and experienced persons who are familiar 
with the content of this operating manual! 
Before  commencing work on the pumping set, ensure it is 
disconnected from power supply, locked out and tagged out. 
As regards pumps operating low- or high-temperature liquids, wait until 
the housing reaches the ambient temperature level. 
 
Before dismantling a pump, close the valve on the discharge and suction inflow 
side, equalise the pump pressure with the surroundings and drain the pumped 
medium. 
 
As regards pumps operating aggressive or hazardous liquids, their 
interior must be rinsed with a neutral liquid or disinfected. The drained 
liquid and washings must be handled inline with applicable regulations. 
As regards pumps with oil-lubricated bearings, drain oil from bearing housings. 
 
In potentially explosive atmospheres it is prohibited to use tool which 
usage may lead to sparks and fire, use non-sparking tools only. 
 
ATTENTION! 
Use only parts purchased in recognised service outlets or directly from 
the manufacturer. Before assembly, new parts must be compared with 
the dismantled parts to make sure they are equivalent and made of the 
same material. 
During work, observe all safety instructions and secure the pump and its 
components against accidental dropping. 
Do not use excessive force. Elements subjected to force, e.g. hit with a hammer, 
must be secured with a pad made of plastic, hardwood or copper.  
It is recommended that, during damaged (e.g. damaged packing) pump 
disassembly, inspection of the damaged element as well as all other details, e.g. 
bearings, should be inspected and replaced if worn.

additionally degreased and smoothed as required.  
Observe the required bolt tightening torques.
